- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or erratic, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points below true peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to hold or overcorrect — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 points.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags 1–3 days behind true trend — align forecast with 1–2 day lagged sentiment or price momentum.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model fails to adjust — force forecast to match sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
